newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll sees France's centre-right retaining power.
newsitem.headline: Poll sees France's centre-right retaining power.

text.p: France's conservatives would retain their absolute majority and the extreme right would fail to enter the National Assembly if a general election, due in a year, were held now, an opinion poll published on Friday found.

The Ipsos survey in the weekly Le Point said the ruling centre-right coalition, which won a landslide victory in 1993, would lose more than a quarter of its deputies but still retain well over half of the assembly's 577 seats.
The poll of 1,741 voters found the main Socialist opposition party would almost triple its parliamentary presence, and the Communists would make slight gains.

The far-right National Front, although polling 15 percent of the vote, would remain barred from parliament by the two-round single-member constituency system which favours larger parties and coalitions, it showed.
The survey gave the following projections, with the current totals in brackets: centre-right coalition 343 seats (477), Socialists 204 (76), Communists 30 (24), National Front 0 (0).
A general election is scheduled for March 1998.
